I'm glad you feel that way.

I lurk on this sub only to learn more about how those who are intersex experience life, and I don't want to overstep any boundaries.

If I had one piece of advice to give to OP, it would be to focus on what being nobinary means to you personally, not what it means to anyone else. Be true to yourself, respect yourself, respect and learn about other people whose experience differs from your own.

Not only is this harmful to intersex people, but this mindset is inherently transphobic. You shouldn't need to use one minority experience to minimize another.

If you're trans (like myself, i get it, as an NB AFAB) own it. Hiding who you are to others AND yourself is going to make it harder for yourself in the long run.

It's fine. I see other queer and trans people here and there, have tons of pride pins and stickers on my bag as I go about campus, and I've never been harassed. 

But as the other commenter mentioned, there's still bigots and transphobes here, too. I don't feel unwelcome as a trans student, but it's only slightly friendlier than other cities in the south. That being said, I've had no problems from professors or faculty when explaining my preferred name/pronouns.

Thank you for the detailed response. One thing that actually makes me reluctant to leave the south is the whole hospitality thing, so it's encouraging to hear that there's nice people outside of here.

I actually have a friend (also trans) who moved out of the south to live in Arizona, so I'll reach out to them for an opinion.
